card.name: Past-tense was/were after a subject
card.fires_on: The word was or were (and sometimes 'and') right after a subject, where a past-tense verb is expected next. Common in label text like 'studies were conducted'.

modes.label: Studies were
modes.description: 'were' after a plural study noun in drug-label sections on trials or toxicology.
modes.example: Clinical pharmacology studies<< were>> conducted to assess the effect of tadalafil

modes.label: General was
modes.description: 'was' after a subject such as who or he in ordinary prose.
modes.example: U.S. Presidents: Everything You Need Who<< was>> the first president to live in the White

modes.label: Linking and
modes.description: 'and' that joins two past or present verb forms, in place of was.
modes.example: it had,<< and>> has, deep-seated roots in perceptions

card.writes: It suppresses the word 'was' itself, so it seems to push the model away from repeating was or were next.
card.plain: It fires right on the was or were that follows a subject, as in 'studies were conducted'.
